text:
maya: Starting canary for index_correction backfill btf-710 on prod. Plan: canary on shard-0 at 5% traffic, monitor 10m, then stagger. requesting lease. @ernie @release-manager

deploybot: Lease granted to canary-runner for job btf-710.canary. config: chunk_size=400, concurrency=1, canary_split=5%, stall_watch=enabled. ETA ~9m. :rocket:

ernie: Will watch p95/p99 + blocking_pids. Abort criteria: sustained long_lock_count >= 2 over 3m OR p99 > 800ms. If abort happens we pin and open rollback plan.

sre-bot: Observability rule armed: if long_lock_rate > 0.5% for 5m -> alert #eng-oncall.

maya: Kicking canary now.

deploybot: Canary progress: 0% -> 12% -> 25%. No alerts.

ernie: Canary healthy so far, p99 ~120ms, no blocking locks.

maya: Ramping to 20% across shard-0 + shard-1 split. Increasing traffic for faster validation.

deploybot: traffic_split updated to 20%.

sre-bot: Alert: shard-1 p99 spiked to 950ms, long_lock_count=3. Auto-pause threshold reached.

release-manager: Hold on abort. Do not trigger global abort yet. Let's rollback traffic to 10% and reduce chunk_size to 200. Prefer containment over full abort for transient issues.

maya: Applying live config: `./deploybot config --job btf-710 --chunk_size 200 --traffic_split 10%`

deploybot: Live config applied. chunk_size=200, traffic_split=10%.

ernie: After rollback, shard-1 p99 dropped to ~300ms and long locks subsided. Good signal.

release-manager: Keep canary longer (+20m). If stable, stage remaining shards in 10% increments every 10m. Drafting release-note: "Canary backfill btf-710 staged; transient lock spike during ramp led to traffic rollback and chunk-size reduction; monitoring extended; no abort."

sre-bot: No incident created. Continuing watch.

maya: I'll attach logs + `pg_stat_activity` snapshot to the runbook and add a runbook recommendation: prefer traffic rollback + chunk reduction for transient ramp spikes; abort only on sustained contention or clear index conflicts.

ernie: Uploaded artifacts and a short timeline. Also recommend adding a preflight that checks for active index maintenance or large autovacuum on target relations.

maya: Agreed. We'll require a successful full rollout canary and 24h stable metrics before any unpin. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
